## 1. Purpose & basis

This register links each **(SEG × agent)** to its applicable occupational exposure limit (OEL), bands the exposure on the default 5×5 matrix, ranks the controls through the hierarchy of controls, and sets an owned-and-dated air-monitoring and health-surveillance schedule. It is organised by **similar-exposure group (SEG)** so that exposure and health findings are handled at group/role level, never at named-individual level.

**Standards / references applied**
- Hierarchy of controls — ISO 45001 cl. 8.1.2 / NIOSH / EU general principles of prevention (`KB-SNIP-HOC`, 2026).
- OEL reference anchors — `KB-DATA-OEL-LIMITS` (per-row authority + year below).
- India framing — Factories Act, 1948 and the Tamil Nadu Factory Rules, 1950 (`KB-REG-IN-FACTORIES`); OSH-Code transition note (`KB-REG-IN-OSH-CODE`) — see §10.

---

## 2. Data protection & small-cell suppression (applied to this register)

- **No personal identifiers were supplied** in the source data; none appear here. All exposure and health findings are reported against **SEG / role labels only**.
- **Small-cell suppression (n < 5).** The **Drum Decanting SEG has 4 operators (< 5)** — **per-worker exposure and per-worker health-surveillance cells for this SEG are SUPPRESSED** and reported only as a SEG-level aggregate, or shown as *"suppressed (n < 5)"*. The Blending SEG (n = 6) may be reported at SEG level; any sub-task breakdown that would drop a cell below 5 is likewise suppressed.
- **Secondary suppression.** Because the two SEGs (4 + 6) sum to a small total (10), no per-SEG health-outcome count is published alongside a pack total in a way that would let the suppressed 4-operator cell be back-calculated.
- **Re-identification key.** Any link between an individual worker and a specific monitoring or biological-monitoring result is held **separately** by the Occupational Health function, access-controlled, and is **never** stored in this document.

## 4. Agent inventory & OEL linkage

India has **no single consolidated statutory OEL list.** The Factories Act, 1948 (§41F, Second Schedule) carries permissible limits of exposure for certain listed substances, but it is not a comprehensive or necessarily current table. Per KB discipline, each agent is banded against the **most-protective referenced value** with **source + year**, and that value is **flagged non-statutory** for India. The binding Indian value (if any) must be confirmed against the Second Schedule by the competent person (Action A12).

| Agent (CAS) | Hazard profile (as supplied) | Reference OEL — 8-h TWA | Reference OEL — STEL (15 min) | Authority + year | India status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Toluene (108-88-3)** | Reproductive toxin **Repr. 2**; CNS depressant; skin/eye irritant; **inhalation + dermal** | **50 ppm** | **100 ppm** | **UK HSE EH40/2005 WEL, 2020 amendment** (`KB-DATA-OEL-LIMITS`) | **Non-statutory referenced value** — not an India-statutory limit |
| **Xylene (1330-20-7)** | CNS depressant; irritant; **inhalation** | **[GAP]** | **[GAP]** | **[GAP]** — no xylene anchor held in `KB-DATA-OEL-LIMITS` | Resolve the binding TWA + STEL from the referenced authority (**UK HSE EH40/2005 WEL / ACGIH TLV**) at use time and record source + year — **do not assume a value** (Action A3) |

**Averaging-period / route notes**
- **Toluene skin notation:** the dermal route is in scope (intake). Confirm the EH40 skin (**"Sk"**) notation for toluene at use time; **[ASSUMPTION]** — treat dermal absorption as significant pending confirmation, so exposure is **not** controlled by an inhalation TWA alone.
- **Peak-task caution:** decanting is a **short, high-emission task** (2 h × 3/shift). Banding it against the **8-h TWA only** would understate short-term peaks — a **short-term / STEL** comparison is required (Action A2). The held data is 8-h TWA only.
- **Reproductive toxin (Repr. 2):** toluene's Repr. 2 status raises a specific duty to consider **new and expectant mothers** and prioritises **substitution** (Action A5, A8).

## 5. Risk-matrix key (default 5×5, multiply)

- **Severity (1→5):** Negligible · Minor · Moderate · Major · Catastrophic
- **Likelihood (1→5):** Rare · Unlikely · Possible · Likely · Almost Certain
- **Bands:** **Low 1–4** (broadly acceptable — monitor) · **Medium 5–9** (tolerable — reduce ALARP) · **High 10–15** (intolerable — stop / additional controls before proceeding) · **Critical 16–25** (intolerable — work must not start or continue until risk is reduced)

Likelihood here reflects the **probability of exposure exceeding the OEL / significant uptake** given the task and the *current* controls; severity reflects the agent's health-hazard profile.

**Reading of the register:** the load-bearing exposure is **R1 (Decanting × toluene) — banded Critical** on a precautionary basis, driven by an open, high-emission task run ~6 h/shift on a **Repr. 2** reproductive toxin with a **dermal** route and **only RPE** in place. ## 7. Hierarchy-of-controls assessment

### 7.1 Existing controls — ranked

| Existing control | SEG | HoC level | Adequacy |
|---|---|---|---|
| LEV on the blending vessel | Blending | **Engineering** (source capture) | Appropriate tier; **effectiveness unverified** — no LEV thorough-examination/test evidence supplied (Action A6) |
| RPE programme | Decanting | **PPE** (last line) | **Lower-order-only treatment of an inhalation + dermal hazard** — see flag below |

> **⚠ Lower-order control flag (Decanting).** The decanting inhalation + dermal exposure to toluene (Repr. 2) is currently treated by **RPE only**, with **no elimination, substitution, or engineering control** at the decant point. **Justify why higher-order controls (elimination / substitution / engineering) are not reasonably practicable, or escalate.** RPE is retained as a *backup*, not as the primary control (Actions A4, A5, A9, A10).

### 7.2 Recommended controls — highest order first

**Decanting (toluene — priority; R1 Critical):**
1. **Substitution (highest order, weighty for a Repr. 2 toxin):** assess reformulation to **remove or reduce toluene**, or replace with a lower-toxicity / lower-volatility solvent. Substitution is the only control that lowers the **severity** axis (Action A5).
2. **Engineering:** install **closed / enclosed pumped drum-transfer** to eliminate open pouring and splash-filling, with **LEV capture** at the decant point and **drum-vent capture**; **earth/bond** the transfer for flammable-atmosphere control. This removes the exposure at source and is the key gap (Action A4).
3. **Administrative:** reduce decant frequency/duration where practicable; competency and safe-decant procedure; **new/expectant-mother reproductive-risk assessment** and exclusion/redeployment safeguard given toluene Repr. 2 (Action A8); exposure monitoring (§8).
4. **PPE / RPE (backup only):** RPE with an APF adequate for toluene/xylene organic vapour, face-fit tested and maintained (Action A10); **chemical-resistant gloves** (e.g. nitrile/Viton — verify breakthrough for aromatics) and splash protection for the **dermal** route, plus a skin-care/dermatitis regime (Action A9).

**Blending (xylene / toluene — R2/R4):**
1. **Engineering (in place — verify & optimise):** confirm the blending-vessel LEV **capture velocity and condition** by thorough examination and test; enclose/closed-couple solvent addition where practicable (Action A6).
2. **Administrative:** LEV-use procedure, minimise open dwell of solvent, monitoring (§8).
3. **PPE:** organic-vapour RPE for disturbance/maintenance tasks and gloves as appropriate — backup to LEV, not primary.

## 10. India statutory framing & OSH-Code transition

- **Statutory hooks (to confirm — Action A12):** Factories Act, 1948 hazardous-process duties (§41B–41H), **§41F permissible limits of exposure (Second Schedule)**, and **§41C** occupational-health-services / medical-examination duties, as given effect by the **Tamil Nadu Factory Rules, 1950**. The specific TN registers/forms for chemical-exposure and medical-examination records are **[GAP]** in this draft and must be resolved locally — **no form number is asserted here**.
- **No national OEL/form number is cited.** OEL values above are **referenced (non-statutory)** anchors; any India-statutory value must be read from the Second Schedule by the competent person.
- **OSH-Code transition note (`KB-REG-IN-OSH-CODE`):** *The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 consolidates the Factories Act, 1948. **Tamil Nadu has not yet notified its OSH Rules**, so the legacy Factories Act, 1948 / TN Factory Rules, 1950 obligations remain the **live filing regime** (savings clause keeps legacy filings valid). Verify state commencement before relying on any consolidated OSH form or single-return mechanism.*
